claim: A minimal GPU-initiated RDMA path issues an 8-byte write in 0.7 microseconds and completes in 4.0 microseconds, while production libraries add up to 4.6 microseconds of issue time on top of that floor.
stance_target: the latency floor of GPU-initiated communication, as a reference for whether a host-staged path can compete
scope_conditions: NVIDIA H100/H200/B200/GB200 with ConnectX-7 InfiniBand; mini-gda vs NVSHMEM IBGDA, NCCL GIN, DeepEP, UCCL-EP, MSCCL++, fabric-lib
quoted_support: A minimal GPU path issues an operation in 0.7 us and completes in 4.0 us; libraries add up to 4.6 us of issue time through queue management, memory ordering, and completion scope, and issue time scales with the SM clock.

claim: A tuned CPU-proxy submission path matches or beats the GPU-initiated path at idle (5.9 vs 6.9 microseconds median round trip), at the cost of a dedicated CPU core whose operating state determines its latency and throughput.
stance_target: the claim that host-mediated communication is not inherently slower than device-initiated communication when the host is properly provisioned
scope_conditions: InfiniBand platform; single unloaded operation; proxy needs a dedicated core
quoted_support: A tuned CPU proxy matches or beats the GPU path at idle, at the cost of a dedicated core whose operating state sets its latency and throughput... A tuned proxy completes within 0.07 us of the minimal GPU path and has a lower median round trip (5.9 vs 6.9 us).

claim: Sharing a communication queue with bulk traffic raises latency by one to three orders of magnitude; a reserved queue recovers one to two orders of magnitude.
stance_target: the claim that mixing gradient traffic with other transfers on a shared fabric destroys latency, which is relevant to DDP overlap design on a single PCIe link
scope_conditions: both GPU-initiated and CPU-proxy submission paths; proxy FIFO shared with bulk traffic
quoted_support: Shared queues degrade under load for both submission paths: a proxy FIFO shared with bulk traffic reaches tens of milliseconds, and a reserved queue recovers one to two orders of magnitude.

claim: All-to-all traffic loses 59% of its NIC message rate at about 3,000 active connections, and Dynamically Connected transport does not remove this decline.
stance_target: the claim that many-peer all-to-all patterns degrade super-linearly with participant count, independent of raw bandwidth
scope_conditions: InfiniBand NIC, 32-PE sweep, RC QPs vs DC transport
quoted_support: At the NIC, active connections cost more when sending and receiving together: a send-only NIC keeps about 242 M msg/s through 32,768 active queues, while all-to-all traffic loses 59% of its rate near 3,000 connections, and Dynamically Connected (DC) transport does not remove this decline.

claim: Communication code can cost up to 37% of a kernel's useful throughput even when it is dormant, by lowering GPU block residency.
stance_target: the claim that adding a communication library to a training kernel has a hidden occupancy cost separate from its bandwidth cost
scope_conditions: GPU kernels with communication code compiled in but unused
quoted_support: Communication code can cost up to 37% of a kernel's useful throughput even when dormant, by lowering block residency.

claim: GPU-initiated transports (IBGDA, GDAKI, NCCL GIN, DeepEP) move submission to the GPU but still require a NIC reachable over PCIe and peer-addressable GPU memory, so they presuppose a fabric capability that a no-P2P consumer box does not have.
stance_target: the repo's claim that the GPU-initiated EP stacks cannot be used on the CMP 170HX box
scope_conditions: NVIDIA datacenter GPUs with ConnectX-7; InfiniBand or NVLink-C2C
quoted_support: Modern GPU-initiated transports like IBGDA and GDAKI instead move this control to the GPU, enabling GPU threads to construct RDMA descriptors and ring NIC doorbells themselves, over PCIe.

claim: Every submission path except a cold IBRC proxy exceeds 90% of line rate by 7 KiB, the size of a DeepSeek-V3 token's FP8 hidden state, so per-token messages are large enough to saturate the link once queued properly.
stance_target: whether MoE token-sized messages can reach line rate, which bounds how much of the EP penalty is message-size rather than bandwidth
scope_conditions: InfiniBand platform, payload sweep to 7 KiB
quoted_support: Every path except a cold IBRC proxy exceeds 90% of line rate by 7 KiB, the size of a DeepSeek-V3 token's FP8 hidden state.
